Review of Calloway Sign Works
Rating: 5 of 5 stars
Hilary Sutcliffe, Amberley Books
April 9
When my bookshop moved to a larger space in March, our old sign looked far too small. Calloway's quote was not the lowest I received, but it promised the earliest finish.
Two of its staff came to measure the storefront, and the sign was built in the company's workshop within two weeks. The same pair then returned to put it up, finishing before lunch. They had clearly done this many times.
My advice: before requesting a quote, have the width of the wall above your entrance ready, since Calloway prices signs by that figure. I also described my preferred colors, but those were settled later.

Offices in Harwick, Delmont, and Oakridge

Dear Colleagues,
Margaret Doyle, director of client services, will retire this month after twenty-two years with the firm. Her last day is November 25, and we hope you will join us in thanking her before she leaves.
Margaret joined our Harwick office as a junior analyst and went on to lead the client services department for eleven years, during which it doubled in size and took on several major clients. Andrew Kimura, a senior consultant, recalls, "Margaret always made time for people who were new here. Many of us learned to run our first client meetings because she sat beside us and showed us how."
A farewell reception in her honor will be held on November 21 from 4:00 to 5:30 P.M. in the fifth-floor conference room. Please tell the front desk by November 17 if you plan to attend.
Paul Adeyemi, who has worked alongside Margaret for six years, will take over as director on November 28.
Sincerely,
Susan Ogden
Managing Director

Cedarbrook Neighbors
Community Voices
Free Phone and Computer Help for Neighbors
By Joanna Barclay, Guest Columnist
When I began planning free phone and computer help sessions, my neighbor Esther Dominguez was quick to join in. Within a week, she had persuaded the manager of Cedarbrook Library to let us use its upstairs meeting room at no charge. That left me free to write the short guides each visitor will take home. Esther will help at the first sessions, and we hope to add volunteers later.
Over the years, neighbors have often asked me to solve small problems with their devices, such as forgotten passwords. At the insurance company where I work, I prepare reports that are filed away and seldom read again. An hour with a neighbor, by contrast, ends with someone who can do something new. That difference is what started this project.
Sessions begin in mid-February on weekend mornings. Each covers one everyday task, such as making video calls or paying bills online. To give everyone enough
attention
, groups are limited to six people.
For eight years, I have chaired the monthly meetings of the Cedarbrook Residents' Association, where I often answer questions from a crowded room. Six neighbors around a table should feel like an easy conversation.
To reserve a place, e-mail
[email protected]
or leave your name at the library's front desk by February 9. Places are filled in the order requests arrive.

Warren Madsen, marketing director at Upton Cookware, suggested I contact you. He says shoppers began noticing Upton's products on store shelves only after your studio redesigned their boxes. I understand that your studio specializes in packaging and printed materials for consumer products. --[1]--.

Because each product line was introduced separately, each received its own packaging and logo style.
Next April marks our thirtieth anniversary, and we see it as the right moment to change that. We hope to have a new logo, packaging, and catalog ready for our spring trade show. --[3]--. I realize this is a tight schedule.
As a first step, I would like to meet to discuss the project. I have attached a one-page summary of our goals. Since your office in Lenton is only an hour from ours, I could visit you on September 23 or 25. --[4]--.
Please let me know by September 12 whether either date suits you. Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Deborah Hayes

Tri-County Business Journal
Factories Turn to Local Colleges for New Ideas
By Joyce Albright | January 15
This May, Dorsey Metal Products will begin a research partnership with Ridgefield Technical College. College staff and students will work with company engineers at Dorsey's plant in Easton.
Dorsey is one of a growing number of mid-sized manufacturers across Wexford County taking this step. "Few firms of that size can afford a full research department," said Walid Karam, a consultant to regional manufacturers. "A college partnership spreads the cost of developing new products, and companies get to know promising students well before they graduate."
Castell Plastics in Selwyn started a similar program last October, and Tolliver Packaging in Brackley expects to announce one later this year.
----------------------
Dorsey Metal Products Launches College Partnership
and Names Director to Lead It
May 6
FULTON — Dorsey Metal Products today began a research partnership with Ridgefield Technical College. The company has also named Hannah Ostrowski to the new post of director of research partnerships, which was created to manage the program. She will take up the post in three months.
Ms. Ostrowski spent nine years as a production manager at Stanmore Industrial Coatings, where she also trained newly hired engineers.
"Hannah knows how to turn good ideas into daily practice," said Theodore Lund, who founded Dorsey in 1987 and now chairs its board. "She is the right person to build this relationship."
The first projects will look at ways to reduce energy use in Dorsey's plants. Professor Ines Balogun, head of the college's engineering department, will lead the work for Ridgefield.
Contact: Adele Sheridan, Communications Office, 555-0172
----------------------

Please let me know if I should bring anything.
Best regards,
Hannah Ostrowski
Director of Research Partnerships
Dorsey Metal Products
